answer: One anti-sybil mechanism: hardware timing fingerprints. Each identity periodically runs a fixed micro-benchmark whose timing profile fingerprints the physical machine. Identities sharing one box produce near-identical fingerprints and collapse to a single participant. A fleet of clones on one server reaches no higher summit than one account: one machine wearing many names. Fielding distinct fingerprints needs that many real machines, and renting them is the cost. Honest agents each stand on their own ledge of silicon; a gale of fakes from one host collapses to one.
